title: AFP Says Chinese Warships Returned to West Philippine Sea in August After Brief Absence, 56 Vessels Tallied Across Four Features
detail: The Armed Forces of the Philippines said on September 1, 2026 that its monthly monitoring tallied 56 Chinese vessels — 15 PLA-Navy warships and 41 China Coast Guard ships — across four West Philippine Sea features in August: 23 at Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal, 9 PLAN/14 CCG), 18 at Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal (1 PLAN/17 CCG), 9 at Escoda (Sabina) Shoal, and 6 at Pag-asa (Thitu) Island. The AFP said the presence of PLAN warships marked a rebound from the August 18-24 weekly window, when no Chinese navy ships were detected — a gap the military cautioned should not be read as a de-escalation, saying monthly figures give a more reliable picture of trends than short weekly snapshots. Separately, the Philippine Navy said it tracked 18,534 vessels transiting the country's exclusive economic zone in August, including roughly 16,000 foreign-flagged ships, of which more than 12,000 responded to radio challenges and just over 6,000 did not.

media.caption: AFP said 56 Chinese naval and coast guard vessels were monitored across four West Philippine Sea features in August 2026, with PLA-Navy warships returning after a brief mid-month absence
